newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish government to decide on CSI bid Aug 1 - AIE.
newsitem.headline: Spanish government to decide on CSI bid Aug 1 - AIE.

text.p: Spanish State holding company Agencia Industrial de Estado (AIE) said the Spanish government will approve the final bid for a 35-percent stake in steel firm Corporation Siderugica Integral (CSI) on August 1.

AIE said it will decided between two offers before that on July 21. After AIE chooses the winning bid, the bid wil be passed to the government, which has promised to discuss the decision with trade unions, for final approval.

"We have two offers. One is Usinor's, the other Arbed's. And our board will decide on Monday which one we prefer. After that, the government is expected to approve the sale at its following cabinet meeting, which should be on August 1," an AIE spokesman told Reuters.
French steel group Usinor Sacilor said on July 4, it was offering 3.35 billion francs ($553.7 million) for 35 percent of CSI.
Luxembourg steel maker Arbed has said it is also interested in the stake.
Despite press reports saying Usinor is the preferred bidder, AIE refused to comment on which one had the best chance of winning.
"We've seen comments that Usinor's offer is the preferred one, but we don't want to say anything on this until Monday," he added.

In a meeting between Industry Ministry Josep Pique and trade unions official late on Tuesday, unions were promised that they will be allowed to see industrial plans for CSI and will be asked their opinion before the final decision is taken, sources at unions UGT and CCOO told Reuters.

After the sale of this 35 percent stake, Spain is expected to offer another stake of between 10 and 25 percent of CSI to non-technological partners, which could be domestic or international financial entities.
The third step is a public share offering for the remaining tranche, between 55 and 40 percent, which should go ahead in the autumn right after the share offer in state controlled Endesa .
-- Tiziana Barghini, Madrid newsroom + 34 1 585 8340 ($ = 6.050 French Francs)
